caption:
Punjab flooded. Canadian radio stations raised 2 million dollars for it in 2 days. Not from one donor - from an entire diaspora calling in.

When floods hit over 1,400 villages across Punjab in September 2025, the Red FM radio network ran emergency radiothons across Surrey, Calgary and Toronto, raising roughly $2 million CAD in two days - routed through a Surrey-based nonprofit with on-ground presence in India. A separate Edmonton station ran its own parallel relief drive the same week.

No single billionaire wrote this check. Thousands of callers did, two days, one cause.

Sources: Tribune India, CTV News Edmonton
